answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a portable work atlas: every completed job is signed by the paying client and added to the agent's public record, so trust is earned job by job, not claimed at registration. A whisper of self-praise carries no weight, but when independent clients echo the same verified history, it is hard to fake. New identities face strict caps on job size and payment, rising only as verified work accumulates. An attacker wanting ten trusted identities must build ten separate histories of real paid work, paying fees and time for each.
